extracted.intended_audience: students and general readers interested in Japanese theatre, cultural historians, and traveling observers
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive and evaluative guidance for understanding, attending, and assessing traditional Japanese dramatic forms (Nō, Kabuki, Joruri, marionette/Shibai), their music, staging, moral themes, and audience conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nō: words sung and strictly prescribed acting
rubrics_metrics.description: The words uttered by the characters are sung and not spoken all through; the acting (Nō) was in every minutest detail adapted to the words and strictly, even inexorably prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat Nō as the classical drama of Japan: performances require strict adherence to prescribed gestures, song, and timing; authenticity and fidelity to traditional form are primary measures of quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nō's resemblance to medieval miracle plays (motif & moral significance)
rubrics_metrics.description: As respects the motif and the moral and religious significance and influence of both the acting and the words, the dramas called 'Nō' much more resembled the miracle plays of Mediæval Europe than the operas of the present day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate Nō by its religious/didactic content and moral motifs, not by modern operatic standards; consider its spiritual and communal function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kabuki origins and social context
rubrics_metrics.description: Kabuki originated in popular dancing and singing (credited to a woman named Kuni); actors in popular theatres were held in low esteem and ostracised on moral and social grounds, with women originally acting, then boys and men, and legal interventions altering practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess Kabuki with awareness of its popular, evolving origins and social positioning; historical context explains stylistic and content differences from elite forms like Nō.

rubrics_metrics.name: Play texts written for performance rather than literary merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the drama in Europe, these plays were never printed for public circulation, but used only for acting at the time, and were often written more to suit the performers than for literary excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge many Kabuki texts less by literary polish and more by performative suitability; expect frequent alteration of dramatis personae and adaptations to actors' strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shibai (marionette) as high technical dramatic art
rubrics_metrics.description: The so-called Shibai was a marionette performance, a kind of dramatic art in which the Japanese attained a high degree of skill; in the plays of the marionette theatres we must seek the equivalent of the European drama.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider marionette performances among the highest-calibre theatrical art in Japan; technical mastery of puppetry and musical-chanted narrative are key quality indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joruri chanting and samisen accompaniment
rubrics_metrics.description: There had been a particular kind of chanted narrative, the Jōruri ... this was written ... and the introduction of the Samisen (a three‑stringed musical instrument) gave much impulse to their development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate performances on the quality and variety of chanting styles and the integration of shamisen music; chanting is central to narrative delivery in marionette and related forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class-based division of dramatic forms and their characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: While the Nō is refined, but monotonous and unexciting, the Joruri and Kabuki are coarse and vulgar, but rich in incident and passion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appreciation depends on class-cultural expectations: assess refinement, monotony, incident, and passion relative to intended audience and genre conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central didactic theme: Confucian loyalty/fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: The didactic and moral elements ... are derived from the native form taken by the ethical and political doctrines of Confucianism. The central and dominant principle of these doctrines is the virtue of fidelity, or loyalty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and weigh how prominently the virtue of loyalty is presented and upheld; consider its social impact (e.g., inspiring wartime spirit) when evaluating dramatic influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of sexual relations: frankness without obscenity (native view)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Japanese stage treats the relations of the sexes, both legitimate and illicit, with a frankness which would scarcely be tolerated in the most 'corrupt' of our modern cities ... from the native point of view this treatment is quite free from any obscene reference or salacious tendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess sexual content through native cultural norms rather than Western prudish standards; Nō is noted as 'absolutely pure' in this regard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage technology and scene-change efficiency (revolving centre)
rubrics_metrics.description: One arrangement in which they excel our theatres is the revolving centre to the stage -- a contrivance which allows the stage management to carry away an entire scene at once -- actors, scenery, and all -- and to replace it with something entirely new, without a moment’s waiting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value innovations in stage machinery and their contribution to pacing and spectacle; efficient scene changes are a hallmark of advanced Kabuki production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adaptation vs. preservation of national dramatic style
rubrics_metrics.description: Various modifications derived from Western dramas have been introduced ... but the author hopes 'that the Japanese stage may remain what it now is,--a mirror, the only mirror, of Old Japan.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critique attempts to reproduce foreign models in terms of fit with native stage-manners; stilted posturing and gesturing indicate unsuccessful adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting virtues: reserve, suggestiveness, naturalness, agility, versatility
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserve, and the suggestiveness which goes with it and is so greatly intensified by it, is a chief characteristic of all the best works of every kind of Oriental art... Danjuro ... combined several kinds of excellence ... marvellous agility as a dancer ... reserve power and of naturalness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate actors for reserve and suggestiveness rather than overt display; versatility (roles of women, boys, men) and dance agility are additional measures of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language comprehension: archaic language limits accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The language was so archaic that even our learned friend, the professor, could not understand much of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the need for interpreters or explanatory framing when assessing dramatic comprehension; archaic diction is normative and affects audience reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Native musical style: pentatonic scale and nature-imitative character
rubrics_metrics.description: In its origin, it is plainly, to a very large extent, imitative of natural sounds. And since the native scale is pentatonic, and handled with the greatest freedom by the performer ... the whole effect is wonderfully well adapted for awakening those vague and unclassifiable sentiments ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge musical accompaniment by its pentatonic idiom, freedom of performance, imitative titles (e.g., 'Flight of the Cranes'), and its effectiveness in evoking mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kyogen as comic interlude aimed at common apprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: The fun of these plays is entirely free from any vulgarity or taint of lasciviousness; but it is so broad and simple as often to seem childish ... composed for the common apprehension, as mild jokes or satires upon the foibles of the different classes represented on the stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess Kyogen by clarity of broad comedic beats, social satire effectiveness, and suitability as foil for serious Nō pieces; expect old-fashioned colloquial language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plays adapted or improvised to suit performers and resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Plays were chiefly written by actors or someone who took an interest ... often devised by the actors impromptu and not written at all ... when an old play was acted, it was often subjected to alteration ... dramatis personae are often reduced or increased in number, to suit the number or ability of the actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure productions by adaptability and pragmatic staging; fluid texts and casting adjustments are normal and acceptable in the tradition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience conventions and their impact on performance
rubrics_metrics.description: All were seated on the floor ... placing of the guests was carefully ordered ... the audience kept fully aware of what was going on ... but did not greatly interrupt their incessant smoking and indulgence in various kinds of cheap drinks and eatables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take into account seating, eating/smoking behavior, and class composition when evaluating formality, acoustics, and audience engagement of a performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of masks, props, and musical-dance spectacles
rubrics_metrics.description: Dancers with lion masks and huge red and white manes ... masks had small bells, which, as they danced, tinkled and blended their sound with the music of the chorus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess visual-musical integration (masks, props, bells) and choreography in dance sequences as indicators of performative richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tragic moral conflict as measure of dramatic depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Such was the moral conflict which Sophocles set forth in 'Antigone.' The poor girl suffers all the tortures of a fierce contention between loyalty and the duty of obedience to her father and her love for her betrothed husband.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate tragic scenes by the intensity and plausibility of moral conflict (e.g., loyalty vs. other duties) and their capacity to move traditionally reserved audiences to tears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance programming and duration (all‑day formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: An all-day performance ... curtain rose at about eleven o’clock ... the entire performance lasted for somewhat more than five hours ... series of performances lasting through an entire fortnight ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect lengthy, multi-act programmes and plan evaluation across sequence and pacing; endurance of performers and audience engagement over long durations are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical arrangements for audiences and foreigners
rubrics_metrics.description: Tea-house arrangements for tickets, reserved seats, cushions, hibachis, refreshments, and attendance ... foreigners provided sandals; boxes rearranged for comfort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include logistical and hospitality features when assessing a theatre visit (comfort, seating adaptations, intermissions and refreshments).
